name: Mary Budden Estate Dining Room
why_it_matters: Dining at the 1899 estate that British missionary Mary Budden bought as a hill home and ran as an orphanage school. Restored by Serena Chopra, it now serves daily set menus indoors or under the deodars — Himalayan cooking re-interpreted from Nepal through Kumaon, included in the room tariff for guests.
insider_tip: Day visitors can request lunch by prior arrangement only — call ahead. The Milky Way dinner runs on clear nights post-October when the sanctuary's no-light bylaw makes the sky non-negotiable.
signature_address: Mary Budden Estate, Binsar Wildlife Sanctuary, Almora district, Uttarakhand 263601

name: The Kumaon Restaurant
signature_dish: millet roti with seasonal mountain greens
why_it_matters: Cantilevered dining room with a handmade fireplace at the boutique 10-room property designed by Sri Lankan architects Pradeep Kodikara and Jineshi Samaraweera of Zowa Architects (Geoffrey Bawa school). Kitchen leans on millet roti, locally foraged chutneys and herbal teas — sustainable luxury in the Bawa idiom.
insider_tip: The dining room is cantilevered out over the hillside — request the corner table closest to the glass wall for the Nanda Devi line at sunset. Non-residents are very rarely accommodated; book dining only as part of a stay.
signature_address: The Kumaon, Kasar Devi Road, near Binsar Wildlife Sanctuary, Almora district, Uttarakhand 263601

name: Khali Estate Restaurant
why_it_matters: The 25-acre heritage bungalow built in 1895 — once owned by Sir Henry Ramsay (Commissioner of Kumaon 1856–84) and visited by Gandhi in 1929 and Vijaylaxmi Pandit in 1935. The restaurant is pure vegetarian, leans Kumaoni, and uses orchard fruit grown on the property.
insider_tip: The estate is pure-vegetarian by house rule — don't ask for chicken. Sit on the lawn for breakfast: you get the snow line of Nanda Devi without leaving your chair.
signature_address: Khali Estate, P.O. Ayarpani, Binsar Wildlife Sanctuary, Almora district, Uttarakhand 263601

name: Bird Song
why_it_matters: The all-day multi-cuisine restaurant at Club Mahindra Binsar Valley — one of the few in-sanctuary kitchens that does both buffet and à la carte and reliably serves a Kumaoni regional thali (bhatt dal, bhang ka murg, lesu bread, lapsi) alongside the standard hill-resort menu.
insider_tip: Non-members can dine here on prior request — easier than at Mary Budden or The Kumaon, and the Kumaoni thali is the order to make. The Golden Oak lounge-bar is the only proper bar inside the sanctuary belt.
signature_address: Club Mahindra Binsar Valley, near Binsar Wildlife Sanctuary, Almora district, Uttarakhand 263601

name: Binsar Eco Resort Kitchen
why_it_matters: Family-run resort kitchen on the Ayarpani ridge that opens to non-guests on prior request — pure vegetarian, mixes Kumaoni staples (bhatt dal, aloo gutke) with Indian-Continental, and bakes its own bread and jams from estate orchards. The most accessible sit-down meal in the Binsar belt for day-trippers.
insider_tip: Call ahead; the kitchen is tariff-included for guests but day-pass meals need a phone booking. There are no independent restaurants in Binsar — this is one of the few in-resort dining rooms that takes outside walk-ins.
signature_address: Binsar Eco Resort, Matena, near Binsar Wildlife Sanctuary, Almora district, Uttarakhand 263601
